I've added `scripts/plot_revenue.py`, and it runs and produces a correct chart. I ran it with `--out /tmp/revenue_check.png`, so no PNG has been added to the repo. After that run I raised the x-margin slightly (0.04 to 0.06) so the "$71,800" label has more room at the right edge. I reran the script after the change but didn't re-open the image.

- **What it draws:** a single-series line chart of monthly revenue from `data/sales.csv`, titled "Monthly revenue, 2026". I looked at the first render and the 12 points match the CSV, with the last value labeled.
- **Dependencies:** it uses only `csv` and `matplotlib` (3.9.4 is installed). pandas isn't installed here, so I avoided it.
- **Usage:** `python3 scripts/plot_revenue.py [--csv PATH] [--out PATH]`.
- **Default output:** `docs/revenue.png`, the path your README already embeds. That file doesn't exist yet, so run the script without `--out` to create it.
- **Styling:** it uses the dataviz skill's reference palette (blue series, light grid, no legend since there's one series).

The CSV includes 2026-12, although today is 2026-11-28. I charted it as given.
